description: Establish humanity's first permanent base at Shackleton Crater rim, South Pole. Harness permanent polar sunlight, mine shadowed ice, extract regolith oxygen, and withstand solar storms.

objectives.description: Deploy 1 Vertical Solar Array (VSAT) on an elevated rim tile
Install 1 Regenerative Li-Ion Battery Storage System
Construct 1 Pressurized Surface Habitat (4-Crew)
Achieve net positive power generation (> 8 kW) and store 50 kWh

tutorialSteps.title: Launch Phase: Rocket & Payload Insertion
tutorialSteps.instruction: Authorize launch aboard the SLS Block 1B with 15,000 kg payload capacity to begin Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI).
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation: dv = Isp * g0 * ln(m0 / mf). Upper stage provides 7.53 km/s dv, exceeding required 5.61 km/s.

tutorialSteps.title: Landing Site: Peaks of Eternal Light
tutorialSteps.instruction: Select Shackleton Crater Rim (South Pole) and touch down. The rim receives >90% continuous sunlight due to the Moon's 1.54° axis tilt.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA LRO / LOLA altimetry identified elevated ridges along Shackleton Rim with persistent illumination and adjacent cryogenic cold traps.

tutorialSteps.title: Deploying Vertical Solar Array (VSAT)
tutorialSteps.instruction: Open the Build Catalog [B] and place a Vertical Solar Array (VSAT) on an elevated rim tile to capture low-incident polar sunlight.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA VSAT masts elevate solar panels 10 meters above the surface to capture sunlight skimming the horizon without ground shadow blockage.

tutorialSteps.title: Energy Storage for Shadow Dips
tutorialSteps.instruction: Construct a Regenerative Li-Ion Battery Storage unit adjacent to the solar array to buffer power during periodic crater rim shadow dips.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: Even on polar peaks, orbital precession causes periodic shadow dips of 8-12 hours when distant mountain massifs occult the Sun.

tutorialSteps.title: Surface Habitation & Life Support
tutorialSteps.instruction: Place an Inflatable Surface Habitat to house your 4 Artemis astronauts. The habitat provides radiation protection and life support interfaces.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA TransHab multi-layer Nextel/Kevlar expandable shells pack compactly inside rocket fairings and inflate to full 120 m³ pressurized living volume.

realDataReference.title: Peaks of Eternal Light at Shackleton Rim
realDataReference.source: NASA LRO / LOLA Topography Data (Mazarico et al., 2011)
realDataReference.explanation: Because the Moon's axis is tilted only 1.54°, high crater rims at the South Pole remain illuminated by the Sun for over 90% of the year. Placing tall vertical solar arrays maximizes power without requiring large batteries.

objectives.description: Construct 1 Pressurized Surface Habitat (4-Crew)
Deploy Power Solution: Deploy Kilopower Nuclear Reactor (intended solution for 354h night) or size battery microgrid >= 2,000 kWh
Survive the 354-hour equatorial lunar night without base blackout (PWR > 0)
Maintain life support oxygen reserves above 50 kg throughout the 14-day night

tutorialSteps.title: Touchdown at Mare Tranquillitatis
tutorialSteps.instruction: Welcome to the historic Apollo 11 landing site. Unlike polar peaks, equatorial maria endure a brutal 354-hour continuous night.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: The lunar synodic month is 29.53 Earth days (~708.7 hours), dividing equatorial locations into 14.75 days of sunlight and 14.75 days of darkness.

tutorialSteps.title: Equatorial Power Strategy
tutorialSteps.instruction: Sustain the base through 354 hours of darkness by deploying a 10 kWe Kilopower Nuclear Fission Reactor (the intended solution within the $2.0M budget). Sizing batteries alone for the full 354h night (>= 2000 kWh) would require 20 battery banks costing $4.97M, proving why NASA requires fission surface power.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA Kilopower (KRUSTY) uses an enriched uranium cast core with Stirling power conversion to provide steady 10 kW electrical power through the 14-day night.

realDataReference.title: Equatorial Lunar Night & Fission Surface Power
realDataReference.source: NASA Glenn Research Center & Los Alamos National Laboratory Kilopower KRUSTY Project
realDataReference.explanation: At Mare Tranquillitatis, the night lasts 354.35 continuous hours (14.76 Earth days), plunging temperatures to -180°C. Sizing chemical batteries for 354.35 hours of continuous 5.7 kW life support requires 2,020 kWh (over 17 metric tons of batteries). NASA's Kilopower (KRUSTY) 10 kWe reactor provides compact, continuous Stirling fission power independent of the Sun.

objectives.description: Construct 1 Thermal Ice Drill & Condenser Rig in the crater cold trap
Extract and store 250 kg of pure water from icy regolith
Maintain power supply to the shadow zone drill (>= 4.5 kW)

tutorialSteps.title: Cryogenic Volatiles in Shackleton Basin
tutorialSteps.instruction: Permanently shadowed crater depressions maintain 40 Kelvin temperatures, trapping ancient water ice. Deploy the Thermal Ice Drill on a shadow tile.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA LCROSS impact plume proved south polar regolith contains 5.5 wt% water ice along with hydrocarbons and ammonia volatiles.

tutorialSteps.title: Vacuum Thermal Sublimation
tutorialSteps.instruction: In hard vacuum, heated ice sublimates directly into vapor without becoming liquid. Sealed condensers capture and purify steam into drinking and propellant tanks.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA TRIDENT / PRIME-1 drill uses rotary-percussive action and thermal heating coils to extract subsurface ice down to 1 meter depth.

realDataReference.title: Thermal Sublimation Extraction in Hard Vacuum
realDataReference.source: NASA PRIME-1 / TRIDENT Drill Specifications (Honeybee Robotics / NASA STMD)
realDataReference.explanation: Liquid water cannot exist in a vacuum; it either freezes or boils into steam. Heating icy regolith under a sealed hood causes sublimation directly into vapor, which is condensed into tanks.

objectives.description: Construct 1 Molten Regolith Electrolysis (MRE) Oxygen Smelter
Extract and store 500 kg of pure O2 from lunar basalt
Maintain positive power grid (> 8 kW) to sustain the 1600°C electrolysis furnace

tutorialSteps.title: Abundant Oxides in Lunar Regolith
tutorialSteps.instruction: Deploy the MRE Oxygen Smelter. Lunar soil contains 40-45% oxygen bound in silicates and ilmenite (FeTiO3).
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center tests prove molten regolith electrolysis can extract metric tons of breathable oxygen and construction metals without bringing consumables from Earth.

realDataReference.title: Oxygen Extraction via Molten Regolith Electrolysis
realDataReference.source: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center ISRU Technology Project
realDataReference.explanation: At 1600°C, direct electrical currents break metal-oxygen bonds in liquid regolith, producing pure oxygen bubbles at the anode and molten iron/silicon at the cathode.

objectives.description: Construct 1 Pressurized Surface Habitat & ECLSS Life Support
Deploy 1 Microwave Sintering 3D Construction Drone to sinter regolith shielding
Build Regolith Radiation Berm shielding (>= 36 cm thickness, >75% GCR/SPE attenuation)
Endure major Solar Particle Event (SPE) keeping crew cumulative dose < 25 mSv

tutorialSteps.title: Solar Cycle 25 Storm Warning
tutorialSteps.instruction: NASA DONKI space weather alert indicates an approaching CME shock. Construct the Microwave Sintering Drone to build protective radiation berms.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: The Moon has no global magnetic field or atmosphere. Unshielded astronauts during an extreme SPE could receive lethal 1-4 Sievert doses without regolith or water shielding.

tutorialSteps.title: Radiation Attenuation & Half-Value Layer
tutorialSteps.instruction: Sintering regolith around the habitat provides exponential shielding. Every 18 cm of lunar regolith halves incident ionizing radiation (HVL = 18 cm).
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA CRaTER measurements confirmed that 36-50 cm of packed lunar soil cuts ionizing radiation exposure by 75-87%, keeping doses well within NASA-STD-3001 career safety limits.

realDataReference.title: Lunar Radiation Protection & Sintered Regolith Shielding
realDataReference.source: NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group (SRAG) & LRO CRaTER Instrument
realDataReference.explanation: Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) and episodic Solar Particle Events (SPE) pose severe cancer and acute radiation sickness risks. Lunar regolith provides effective mass shielding with a half-value layer (HVL) of approximately 18 cm.

objectives.description: Deploy 1 Pressurized Rover Garage & Charging Bay
Drive VIPER-class prospecting rover >= 2,000 meters into cold trap
Locate volatile cryogenic water ice concentration >= 5.0 wt%
Construct Deep Space Comms Dish for telemetry downlink

realDataReference.title: VIPER Volatiles Prospecting Architecture
realDataReference.source: NASA Ames Research Center VIPER Mission Science Team
realDataReference.explanation: VIPER utilizes the Neutron Spectrometer System (NSS) and NIRVSS spectrometer to identify hydrogen concentrations beneath shadowed lunar regolith.

objectives.description: Construct 1 Zero-Boil-Off Cryogenic Propellant Storage Depot
Construct 1 Thermal Ice Drill & Condenser Rig in shadow cold trap
Produce and accumulate >= 5,000 kg cryogenic propellant in depot storage

realDataReference.title: Lunar In-Situ Propellant Production (ISPP)
realDataReference.source: NASA Glenn CFM Portfolio & STMD In-Situ Resource Utilization Project
realDataReference.explanation: Mining water and splitting it into LOX/LH2 turns the Moon into a deep space refueling station, drastically reducing launch mass from Earth.

objectives.description: Construct 1 Pressurized Surface Habitat (4-Crew)
Sinter radiation protective regolith berm >= 36 cm thickness around habitat
Shelter crew and survive extreme Solar Particle Event keeping cumulative dose < 25 mSv

realDataReference.title: Extreme Solar Particle Events & Sintered Regolith Shielding
realDataReference.source: NASA CRaTER Instrument on LRO / DONKI Database
realDataReference.explanation: Major X-class flare SEP events produce extreme proton fluxes. 36 cm of sintered regolith provides two half-value layers (75% attenuation), keeping crew doses safe.

objectives.description: Construct 1 High-Gain Deep Space Comms Dish atop Malapert Mountain
Construct 1 Zero-Boil-Off Cryogenic Propellant Storage Depot
Stockpile >= 3,000 kg cryogenic propellant ready for Lunar Gateway ascent
Maintain >= 600 kg purified water reserves

realDataReference.title: Malapert Mountain Direct Earth Line-of-Sight & Gateway Logistics
realDataReference.source: NASA LOLA Elevation Map & Artemis Architecture Definition Document
realDataReference.explanation: Malapert Mountain's 5 km altitude offers uninterrupted line-of-sight to Earth and ideal trajectory geometry for orbital propellant transfers to the Lunar Gateway.

objectives.description: Construct 1 Pressurized Surface Habitat (4-Crew)
Deploy 1 ECLSS Closed-Loop Life Support Processor
Deploy 1 Kilopower KRUSTY Nuclear Fission Reactor (10 kWe continuous)
Sinter protective regolith berm (>= 36 cm thickness)
Produce and stockpile >= 5,000 kg cryogenic propellant for crew return vehicle
Complete full 180-day sustained expedition surviving dynamic space weather

tutorialSteps.title: Expedition Artemis: 180-Day Architecture
tutorialSteps.instruction: Commander, your crew of 4 will occupy Artemis Base Camp for 6 months. Deploy continuous nuclear baseload, life support, and sintering drones immediately.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: NASA's Artemis Plan establishes sustained lunar exploration with 30-to-180-day human surface stays at the lunar South Pole.

tutorialSteps.title: Dynamic Hazard Milestones
tutorialSteps.instruction: Mission telemetry forecasts: Day 30 Micrometeorite impact requiring module repairs, Day 70 Extreme SPE storm requiring >= 36 cm berm and crew shelter, and Day 120 secondary impact.
tutorialSteps.whyThisIsReal: Long-duration stays encounter cumulative environmental hazards. Multi-layered defense (regolith shielding, automated repair, closed-loop ECLSS) is mandatory.

realDataReference.title: Sustained Artemis Base Camp Architecture
realDataReference.explanation: Validates the long-term human presence blueprint: continuous nuclear/solar baseload, 90%+ ECLSS recycling, in-situ water/LOX propellant production, and sintered regolith shielding.
